defaultRequirement: Let users upload files to Google Drive, list and read their files, and delete files the connector created.
summary: Upload and per-file access are straightforward with the recommended drive.file scope. Reading every file in a user's Drive needs a restricted scope, which brings Google verification and possibly a paid security assessment. That is usually the biggest cost and delay.

capabilities.label: Upload / create files
capabilities.conditions: Works with the non-sensitive drive.file scope. The app can then access the files it creates.

evidence.title: Choose Google Drive API scopes (drive.file: recommended, non-sensitive)

capabilities.label: List and read files
capabilities.conditions: Depends on which files are needed. Answer the question above.

capabilities.label: Update files
capabilities.conditions: With drive.file, only files the app created or the user opened/shared with the app (for example through the Google Picker).

capabilities.label: Delete files
capabilities.conditions: files.delete skips the trash and is permanent. Moving to trash is usually safer. The user must have permission to delete the file; in shared drives this needs an elevated role.

evidence.title: files.delete reference (permanent vs. trash behaviour — re-check before quoting)

clarifications.question: Which files does the connector need to read?
clarifications.why: This one answer decides between a scope that needs only basic verification and a restricted scope that needs Google review and possibly a security assessment.

options.label: Only files the connector created, or that the user picks

effects.conditions: Use drive.file plus the Google Picker for user-selected files. Non-sensitive scope: basic verification only.
Covered by drive.file for the same set of files.

options.label: Every file in the user's Drive

effects.conditions: Needs drive.readonly or drive, which are restricted scopes. Requires restricted-scope verification. If the data is stored on or sent through your servers, a third-party security assessment is also required. Only certain app types are allowed to use these scopes.

options.label: Files across the whole company (admin / background sync)

effects.conditions: Use a service account with domain-wide delegation, granted by the client's Google Workspace super admin. Only works for Google Workspace customers, not personal Gmail accounts.

auth.recommended: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with offline access (refresh token) and the drive.file scope
auth.why: Narrowest scope that fits most connectors, and the lightest verification path.
alternatives: Service account + domain-wide delegation for company-wide background access (Workspace admins only).
Internal OAuth app (user type 'Internal') if only the client's own Workspace users will connect. Google verification is not needed for internal apps.

blockers.title: Google OAuth app verification
blockers.detail: Apps used by people outside your Google Workspace organization need verification. Restricted scopes need restricted-scope verification and possibly a paid security assessment from an approved assessor.
blockers.resolution: Pick the narrowest scope first. Prepare privacy policy, homepage, and a demo video. Start verification early. Treat duration as unknown.

blockers.title: Refresh tokens expire after 7 days while the app is in 'Testing'
blockers.detail: External apps whose consent screen is in Testing status get refresh tokens that expire after 7 days. Background jobs will silently stop working.
blockers.resolution: Expect weekly re-consent during testing, or publish the app (In production) before running long background tests.

blockers.title: Domain-wide delegation needs a Workspace super admin
blockers.detail: Only needed if company-wide background access was chosen.
blockers.resolution: Send the prepared request with the service account client ID and exact scopes.
blockers.handoff: Hi! To build {requirement}, we need domain-wide delegation for our service account. In the Admin console go to Security > Access and data control > API controls > Domain-wide delegation, and add client ID <CLIENT_ID> with scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly. Reply if you'd prefer a narrower approach.

alternatives.option: drive.file + Google Picker so users choose files
alternatives.doesNotCover: Automatically discovering files the user never picked

alternatives.option: Move files to trash (recoverable for a period)

engineering.assumptions: drive.file scope, standard OAuth, Picker integration.

waiting.notes: Basic verification: usually days. Restricted scopes and security assessment: weeks, and the assessment has a cost. Internal apps: none.

uncertainty: Scope choice depends on the client's answer above
Verification timelines are set by Google and not guaranteed

tasks.title: Create a Google Cloud project and enable the Drive API
tasks.detail: Any Google account works for testing.
tasks.doneWhen: Drive API shows as 'Enabled' in the Cloud console.

tasks.title: Pick the narrowest scope
tasks.detail: Use the answer to 'Which files does the connector need to read?'. Prefer drive.file.

tasks.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen
tasks.detail: Choose Internal (same Workspace only) or External. Add app name, support email, and scopes.

tasks.title: Create an OAuth client ID (Web application)
tasks.doneWhen: You have a client ID and secret stored as environment variables.

tasks.title: Implement authorization code flow with access_type=offline
tasks.detail: Store the refresh token encrypted. Access tokens are short-lived.

tasks.title: Add the Google Picker (if using drive.file for existing files)
tasks.detail: Lets users choose files and grants your app access to them.
tasks.doneWhen: A picked file can be read by the connector.

tasks.title: Prove scope limits
tasks.detail: With drive.file, try files.list. You should only see app-created and picked files. Record the result.
tasks.doneWhen: Result recorded in the Evidence tab.

tasks.title: Submit for verification (External apps)
tasks.detail: Privacy policy, homepage, domain verification, and scope justification. Add a demo video for sensitive/restricted scopes.
tasks.doneWhen: Verification submitted; status tracked as 'Waiting for external party'.
